question: m07
q: What rate are owner-occupiers actually paying on new variable loans, compared with the advertised rate?

transcript.answer:
In August 2026, owner-occupiers took out new variable-rate loans at an average of **about 6.2%**. That's well below the advertised rates for the same month.

**August 2026**
| Rate | % p.a. | How far above the 6.2% actually paid |
|---|---|---|
| Actual rate on new owner-occupier variable loans (RBA F6, all lenders) | **6.2** | n/a |
| Advertised discounted variable rate (banks, RBA F5) | 6.80 | about 0.6 points |
| Advertised standard variable rate (banks, RBA F5) | 8.77 | about 2.6 points |
| RBA cash rate target (monthly average) | 4.35 | n/a |

- **Almost nobody pays the standard advertised rate.** New borrowers pay about 2.6 points less than the 8.77% headline rate. On a $600,000 loan, that's roughly $15,000 a year in interest.
- **New borrowers also beat the advertised discounted rate by about 0.6 points.** Lenders are still giving extra discounts to win new business.
- **New and existing borrowers now pay the same.** Existing variable-rate owner-occupiers were also paying about 6.2% in August 2026. In early 2026, new loans were slightly cheaper (5.7% vs 5.8% in February; 5.9% vs 6.0% in March), but that gap has gone.
- **Discounts have held up through the rate hikes.** Since January 2026, the cash rate has risen about 0.75 points (3.60% to 4.35%) and the advertised discounted rate rose 0.75 points (6.05% to 6.80%). The actual rate on new loans rose about 0.7 points (5.5% to 6.2%), so lenders passed the increases on almost in full.

The advertised rates are available up to September 2026, still at 8.77% and 6.80%. The actual-rate data only goes up to August 2026 and is rounded to one decimal place.
